incbot: :rotating_light: Paginated alert: multiple egress retransmits observed from AZ11 -> region-west DNS (IPv6). Severity: potential customer impact. Paging oncall.

maria (oncall): I'm on it. Paging net-sre.

alex (net-sre): on call, pinging infra metrics now. Any reported customer hits or just internal telemetry?

maria (oncall): got 3 support tickets (prod customers) reporting high 5xx for websocket/streaming endpoints. All triggered for clients with IPv6-preferred stacks.

zach (eng-runtime): logs show spikes of connection resets when clients use v6 endpoints. IPv4 looks fine. Could be PMTUD or path MTU.

kim (sre-lead): can you share packet stats / retransmit counts? Need quick blast radius.

alex (net-sre): grabbing pcap and counters. From host egress in AZ11 I see high ICMPv6 PTB suppression and repeated SYN retransmits.

alex (net-sre): snippet:
```
> rtt 120ms, retransmits 5-7/s, icmp6 type=2 code=0 (Packet too big) suppressed: yes
> if_mss: 1452
```

maria (oncall): customers impacted: three active customers on Dedicated behind load balancers in AZ11 (IDs obfuscated). Impact: degraded streaming, reconnect loops. Marking P1 for customer-facing degradation.

jordan (product): which workloads? Are these internal demos or paying customers?

maria (oncall): paying customers on dedicated capacity and a web SaaS customer with IPv6-first mobile clients.

kim (sre-lead): initial mitigations: 1) clamp MSS on egress LB to 1220 for IPv6 paths 2) advertise IPv4 preference to clients via DNS TTL low / dualstack steering 3) shift traffic away from AZ11 to AZ12 if immediate.

alex (net-sre): MSS clamp command applied on LB pool for IPv6-only egress: `ip6tables --set-mss 1220` (config pushed). Monitoring.

zach (eng-runtime): can we temporarily disable IPv6 on the affected frontend for dedicated customers? That will force IPv4 and should bypass path.

maria (oncall): if we do that we should coordinate with product/support for messaging. But do it if it fixes the impact quickly.

alex (net-sre): a/b test: I updated route policy to prefer v4 for the troubled VIPs -> immediate drop in retransmits on telemetry.

incbot: Incident declared: INC-2026-0427-AZ11-V6MTU. Incident channel created and pinned.

maria (oncall): manuel@support please prep customer comms draft. I will coordinate with sales for affected accounts.

zach (eng-runtime): runtime team confirms that when IPv6 is forced to IPv4, session stability returns within 30s. Rolling a short-term DNS steering plan.

kim (sre-lead): ok folks: primary mitigation = steer clients to IPv4 and clamp MSS on IPv6. Secondary = traffic shift AZ11->AZ12 for dedicated pools. Execute.

alex (net-sre): initiated traffic shift of 25% -> AZ12 now. Watching per-AZ errors.

alex (net-sre): metrics: AZ11 error-rate dropped from 12% -> 4% after MSS clamp. AZ12 holding steady.

maria (oncall): any indications of hardware flaps or router MTU mismatch on provider peering?

alex (net-sre): talking to provider NOC: they report partial MTU regression on a peering link impacting jumbo frames across an IPv6 path. It responds with ICMPv6 PTB but our suppression logic plus some middleboxes drop those probes leading to PMTUD failure.

zach (eng-runtime): yeah that matches. If PTB gets suppressed, established flows retransmit but never learn smaller MTU.

kim (sre-lead): assign action items: provider escalation (alex), permanent MSS clamp/MTU guard on borders (kim), eval fallback policy to force IPv4 for specific customers when v6 path unstable (zach). Maria coordinate customer comms.

jordan (product): flagged for postmortem: add eval for v6 preference heuristics in Optimize to avoid sudden customer regressions.

alex (net-sre): provider NOC applied a peering fix approx 5m ago, we see progressive recovery. PTB seen -> blackholed now cleared.

maria (oncall): customers reporting improved connectivity. Support closing tickets as resolved if stable for 10 minutes.

incbot: update: system metrics show 95th percentile latency returned to normal for AZ11 v6 paths.

zach (eng-runtime): rolling back forced IPv4 steer for non-impacted customers; will keep MSS clamp in place for 2h while we monitor.

kim (sre-lead): good. Let's not remove clamp until provider confirms MTU stability end-to-end. Also we need a permanent guard: auto-detect PTB suppression and fallback to IPv4 earlier.

maria (oncall): customer impact summary for pager: P1 (limited to AZ11 customers with IPv6-preferred clients). Affected ~3 customers, transient, mitigated by IPv4 steer + MSS clamp + traffic shift. No data loss reported.

jordan (product): suggested customer note template: short explanation + steps we took + ETA for postmortem. I'll draft.

alex (net-sre): leaving traceroutes and pcaps in the incident folder: `s3://redwood-incidents/1800123456/`.

maria (oncall): handoff to morning oncall in 40m. kim please own postmortem and blameless RCA.

kim (sre-lead): will own. Initial action items: (1) add MSS clamp automation on egress LBs for IPv6 (2) run probe suite to detect PTB suppression early (3) update routing fallback heuristics.

zach (eng-runtime): I'll start a ticket to add v6-fallback in runtime and add end-to-end tests for dualstack PMTUD.

jordan (product): notify customer success + account teams now.

maria (oncall): thanks team. I'll archive the channel after transfer. If any regression alerting fires, ping with `@maria (oncall)`.

incbot: Incident INC-2026-0427-AZ11-V6MTU status: mitigated -> monitoring. Auto-close scheduled after 4 hours without regression.

maria (oncall): last note: support to follow up with the three affected customers individually. Logged in incident tracker.

kim (sre-lead): postmortem owner, will request logs and timeline. Expect initial draft within 48 hours.

zach (eng-runtime): thanks all. Closing the loop.
